mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding 3 months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises by >0.5% q/q.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5.5% for two consecutive months signals a late-cycle labor market tightening, which increases wage pressures and reduces corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 5.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by >2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months signals a manufacturing slowdown, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month by >1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during three consecutive months of >1% INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and accelerating inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% signals a sudden acceleration in labor market tightness, which raises wage growth and input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as markets reassess margin pressure.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly negative following a >1% monthly increase in PAYEMS.

mechanism_narrative: A co-movement between real retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) both falling below their 6-month moving averages signals a synchronized weakening in consumer and housing demand, which reduces revenue and capex for broad swathes of the economy and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both RSAFS and HOUST fall below their 6-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for three consecutive quarters signals a secular demand shortfall, which erodes earnings expectations and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of other macro conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during three consecutive quarters of GDPC1 < 1% annualized.
